research_rationale:
EO 9204 (July 21, 1942, Franklin D. Roosevelt), titled Coordination of Federal Activities Affecting the Fishery Industry, read in full in the held Federal Register text (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9204.txt; 7 FR 5657, PDF pages 1-3; machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, with the contents pages of the same issue interleaved between paragraph 3 and its last lines). Identity: the extracted page carries the heading Executive Order 9204 and the register title, the date line July 21, 1942, and F. R. Doc. 42-6998 filed July 23, 1942. Inventory: the order has a preamble (authority under Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941, and purposes) that commands nothing, then numbered paragraphs 1, 2 (with subparagraphs (a) and (b)), 3 and 4; the six clauses of the dossier inventory cover every operative paragraph and I confirm the inventory is complete. First end: Executive Order 9649 of October 29, 1945, held in the repository as a Federal Register text, terminates the Office of Fishery Coordination, established pursuant to EO 9204, together with the office of Fishery Coordinator, and directs the Secretary of the Interior to wind up the Office's affairs. With the Office and the Coordinator gone, every clause of EO 9204 lost its subject: paragraph 1 created them, paragraphs 2 and 3 direct and equip the Office, and paragraph 2(a)'s duty on other agencies to designate liaison officers exists only to keep the Office informed. Paragraph 4 states the order's duration and commands nothing itself. All six clauses are therefore recorded as ended on 1945-10-29, and the whole order ends on that date. Paragraph 4 says the order continues so long as Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941, remains in force. That condition had not failed before the end: EO 9649 itself, signed on 1945-10-29, cites Title I of the Act as its authority. The statute text is not held, so the claim does not rely on when Title I expired.

savings.reason: EO 9649 authorizes and directs the Secretary of the Interior to wind up the affairs of the Office and to use its personnel, records, property and funds for that purpose and for carrying out functions vested in him by Food Directive No. 2 of the Secretary of Agriculture and later delegated to the Fishery Coordinator. Those winding-up and Food Directive functions continue under EO 9649 and the Directive, not under EO 9204; anything the Office did while it existed is an accrued effect.
